messages:
alex: FYI a Zephyr customer is seeing sustained 429s and long tail latency during a traffic spike on their Dedicated pool. Autoscaler didn't react fast enough.
priya: Can you paste repro steps and a request_id? any recent config changes?
alex: Repro steps from customer: run a 120s churn load with ~60 concurrent connections hitting /generate. curl example they sent:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/dedicated/zephyr/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"input":"test"}'
```
request_id: rz-20260312-8842
They see queueing then 429s, start_time ~2026-03-12T14:05Z.
infra-bot: Alert: dedicated-pool-zephyr queue_length=78, 5xx_rate=0.03, scale_events=0 in last 60s
jamie: Quick checks: what's min_replicas/max_replicas and warmup_delay? common culprit is low min + long warmup or insufficient headroom.
alex: Config pulled from control plane:
```
min_replicas: 2
max_replicas: 40
warmup_seconds: 25
scaling_window: 60s
target_concurrency_per_replica: 20
```
alex: With target concurrency 20 and 60 concurrent connections sustained we should scale to 3, but queue length suggests provisioning lag or provisioning blocked.
maria: Any pending capacity or quota errors at infra level? Image pulls, IAM, or billing blocks can stall new instances.
alex: Customer's account had a transient billing hold earlier today; CS says it was cleared at 14:02Z but timing is tight. customer-success-liz: I confirmed they updated card at 14:00 and got "payment processed" email.
priya: Can you check provisioning logs and allocator events for the pool between 14:04-14:08?
alex: paste from allocator log (trimmed):
```
[14:04:10] allocate_request pool=dedicated-zephyr desired=3 -> launching 3
[14:04:12] api: reserve_gpus -> ok
[14:04:14] kube: create_pods -> accepted
[14:04:40] kube: pod zephyr-2 stuck Pending -> FailedScheduling (insufficient resources)
[14:05:05] allocator: retry provisioning after backoff 30s
```
jamie: FailedScheduling = noisy-neighbor / cluster capacity. Which host type? are we hitting node-level GPU shortage.
alex: Pool is on g5x2 nodes. Current cluster utilization shows 95% GPU utilization in region.
maria: That explains the stall. Autoscaler thought it could schedule but underlying infra had no free GPUs; backoff blocked further provisioning.
priya: Quick mitigation ideas: 1) temporarily increase min_replicas to keep warm pods 2) enable burst capacity (if account has burst quota) 3) hot-fallback to a lower-memory model variant for the customer 4) manual slot reserving with ops
jamie: Also reduce warmup_seconds to 5 for this workload to avoid long slow ramps.
alex: I did a manual override: set min_replicas=6 and kicked a prewarm job for Zephyr pool at 14:09Z. queue_length dropped from 78 -> 12 within 40s, 429s stopped.
customer-success-liz: Customer confirms error rate dropped and app recovered. They were pretty unhappy during the window.
priya: Next steps: we should add an alert when schedule failures > 0 for a pool and queue_length > 20 for > 60s. Also correlate billing holds with provisioning attempts.
jamie: Ops follow-up: check cluster capacity in us-west-2 and consider adding spare nodes for Dedicated pools during business hours. I'll file infra ticket.
maria: Noise neighbor mitigation: cap per-tenant node allocation or preemptive isolation for high-SLA customers.
alex: I'll document repro steps and the mitigation we applied in the support ticket. tagging this thread for postmortem.
infra-bot: Ticket created: INFRA-4821 "us-west-2 dedicated pool capacity shortage causing provisioning stalls"
priya: Great. assign owners and add runbook item to ensure min_replicas recommendations for bursty customers.
alex: Thanks everyone. Will follow up with timeline and root cause analysis in the ticket. :thumbsup:"
